diagnostic_interpretation: Probe1 failed before tests because formatter include sorting placed the accessed suite before its parent event fixture. The dependent include group fixes this construction error; failed build logs are retained.

Probe2 independently measures 40 native outcomes per SDK/core and compares 40 direct-owner runs. Every raw observation passes; each owner group has 24 State mismatches and no RAM mismatch. Four event kinds each expose four RO CR2 differences (descriptor start versus byte+5) and two initially-clear-D alias cache differences (native CS.base 0x630000 versus old owner 0x230000).

The descriptor-A-preset control retains PTE.D=0 and CS.base 0x230000. Page A/D-preset controls distinguish the returned descriptor image without attributing all observations to a unique hidden microarchitectural width.

Green1 passes all original/direct/generated/watchpoint/ordinary-resume State and RAM checks. Full-mode has 48 software completion-count assertions per SDK that incorrectly inherited zero from the predecessor fault test. Resumed successful software entry completes once; its assertion is corrected without changing production behavior.

Green2 has only 48 newly-added assertions reading the instruction-execute completion field on a direct event-resume result. The event completion receipt is Delivery.SoftwareCompleted, also consumed by the full-mode owner; the test is corrected to inspect that receipt. All State/RAM/debug outcomes already agree.

Cross-line accessed probes from the predecessor evidence still terminate in KVM INTERNAL_ERROR_SIMUL_EX during #AC delivery; they are failed diagnostics, not architectural guest outcomes. No host split-lock setting was modified.

native_oracle.method: Fresh pinned KVM VM/vCPU per case; two initial SREGS writes and no intermediate rewrites. KVM_PRE_FAULT_MEMORY covers both disjoint physical regions. Native/model inputs have identical code exit-page A bits. Compare the complete represented State and every byte of both main RAM and the alias table without masks.
limitations: Pinned local Intel P/E cores only; no inference of a processor binding from the production host.
The self-alias descriptor lies within one cache line. Cross-line/split-lock, concurrent CPUs/DMA/MMIO and cross-page fragment publication are not qualified by these observations.
Original hardware executions are uninterrupted. Backing, permissions and journal-mutation cases are software contract tests, compared with uninterrupted software executions.

coverage: INT80, INT3, explicit IRQ and NMI cover aligned high-canonical and last-qword descriptors with A clear, writable/read-only leaves, and six self-alias A/D/descriptor-A/read-only controls.

HighC and LLVMC, host-x64 Clang and NeverC, O0/O2 execute 320 original/generated complete State/RAM comparisons per SDK. Debug descriptor-write ranges are independently compared with original guest debug registers.

The event owner validates the initial descriptor, prepares one supervisor write transaction, reads exactly its physical fragments after A/D effects, sets A and commits. Hidden CS uses that fresh image; pre-existing return/selector transactions remain independent.

A distinct appended journal tag stores the committed image. Replay returns it without reading/writing or repeating observer effects. Invalid tag/width/write/value combinations reject before controls or effects, and valid-looking ordinary-store/RMW mismatches reject at replay.

96 event resume comparisons per SDK cover initial read backing, physical read-only then write-only descriptor backing, first/partial frame backing, read-only alias table after page A/D preset, and a frame overwrite of the descriptor before the next missing slot. Lower and ordinary resumed contexts equal uninterrupted state/RAM; NMI acceptance and instruction budget survive.

Eight software debug-retention comparisons per SDK preserve the descriptor write match through first/frame-overwrite backing stops and repeated resume, then enter exactly one following DB for each event kind. Original A=0 write watchpoints report B0/DB for INT80, INT3, IRQ and NMI; descriptor A=1 controls do not.
96 full-mode comparisons per SDK reconstruct contexts across the same six stops. Pending accepted event work resumes without a second instruction attempt or external acknowledgement.
boundaries: NeverC remains host/source x64. Guest widths do not add a compiler target.
Both SDKs replay the full paged-source, legacy-source, shared event/native paging, low instruction-boundary and SDK regression suites.
Cross-line event update/split-lock and further mode/machine-state owners remain unqualified. Software SMM/SGX, unbound asynchronous producers and physical SGX qualification remain open.
Production LLVM remains neverd-llvm-v23.0.0-r6. No final release, pin or source gitlink change.
